key_insight: This paper replaces sample-wise RL rewards with distribution-wise rewards to better align generative models with the target data distribution and reduce reward hacking, mode collapse, and visual artifacts.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical path to more reliable finetuning of visual generative models when image quality, diversity, and stability matter in downstream engineering workflows.
method: Use distribution-wise rewards instead of evaluating each generated sample independently.
Introduce a subset-replace strategy to estimate rewards efficiently by updating only a small generated reference subset.
Apply RL to optimize post-hoc model merging coefficients to reduce train-inference inconsistency from SDE-based RL.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved FID-50K on multiple base models, including SiT from 8.30 to 5.77 and EDM2 from 3.74 to 3.52, alongside better perceived quality and diversity.
watch_item: Estimating distribution-wise rewards and managing subset-replace updates may still add implementation complexity and require careful tuning to avoid unstable optimization.
paper_title: Optimizing Visual Generative Models via Distribution-wise Rewards
